quest.name: The Ashen Penitent
quest.text: Peace, wanderer. Peace... though you have known little of it.

I am Brother Ashen. I keep the candles for souls that were cut short - and lately, too many of them carry your name. I do not judge you. I only ask: will you walk the Ashen Road? Four candles burn for the slain in the wild places. Kneel at each and pray, and their weight may lift from you. But hear the vow: until the last candle is lit, you will raise your hand against no one, and you will not fall.
The first candle burns not far from here; your radar will guide you. When you reach it, sit and pray. The slain may come to test you - lay them to rest first. And remember the vow.
Walk the Ashen Road. Your radar shows the first candle.
The faces of the slain gather around the flame...
The slain will not hear your prayer while they walk. Lay them to rest.
The candle flares. One name grows quiet.
Another candle calls. Follow your radar.
You raised your hand again. The candles gutter out.
You fell on the Ashen Road. The candles gutter out.
Go gently.
The candles will wait. So will I.
I will light a candle for you anyway.
Then I will pray for them alone.
Four candles burn steady. The names are quieter now - not forgotten, but quieter. Your stain is washed away. Go, and carry less than you did.
Walk lighter, friend.

quest.name: Crown of Blood

echo.name: Echo of Sir Aldric the Unyielding
echo.line: A thousand duels, and you still think steel is enough?

echo.name: Echo of Grond the Twice-Born
echo.line: Cut me down. I dare you.

echo.name: Echo of Valdis, the Last Duelist

quest.text: So. The one whose name is whispered in every arena.

I am Valdis - or what is left of him. Once I was the last duelist standing in Aden, and the blood of a thousand rivals crowned me. You have walked that same road. The dead duelists remember you, as they remember me, and they want to know if you are worthy of the crown. Face their echoes - four of them, one after another, here and now. Leave the circle and you forfeit.
Stand where you are. They will come to you, one by one. Each fought in their own way. Learn it, or fall.
Sir Aldric cannot be harmed while his wards stand!
Every breath you hold, I take back.
You fled the circle. The crown waits for someone braver.
Then begin.
The dead are patient.
Another time, champion.
Then the crown stays with the dead.
The echoes bow. The Crown of Blood is yours - and its weight, too. Wear it well.
Until we meet in the arena beyond.

quest.name: Grudge of the Horde
quest.text: Hrr. You. You smell of orc blood.

I am Ugrash, cast out of my tribe for speaking against the Warlord. Listen, man-thing - no, listen. You have killed many of my kin. I do not weep for them; they followed Grukk. But Grukk has noticed you. He swore a blood-grudge, and his avengers are already on your trail. You cannot hide from it. But you can end it. Let them come. Break them. And when Grukk himself comes for you - and he will - put him in the ground.
Go about your hunt. They will find you - three times. Then he comes. In towns they will not dare; outside, they will.
The hunt is on - and you are the prey.
War drums, somewhere close...
Grukk's avengers!
The avengers fall. The drums go quiet... for now.
The ground shakes. Grukk is coming.
You! The one who wears my warriors' blood!
Warlord Grukk has found you!
Run all you like. Grukk always finds his prey!
Go. Be strong.
Hrr. The grudge will not wait forever.
Hrr. Deaf, like Grukk.
Then Grukk will find you anyway. Ha.
Grukk is dead? Then the grudge dies with him, and my tribe can choose a new path. My people owe you, man-thing. Take this.
Strong. Very strong. Ha!

quest.name: Death's Ledger
quest.text: Ah. There you are. Again.

Mortis, clerk of the Reaper, at your service. Do you know how many times I have written your name in the Ledger? Too many. And every time, you slipped back out. Each return tore off a sliver of your soul, and those slivers drift through the world as wisps - lonely, lost and frankly cluttering my books. Gather five of them before they fade and I shall balance your account. Be warned: the Reaper's hounds do not like to see a soul taken back.
The wisps drift away from those who chase them, so be quick and cut them off. Your radar shows where they flicker. Two may fade; no more.
Find the wisps of your soul. Your radar will show them.
A pale wisp flickers nearby. Your radar marks it.
...warm... I remember being warm...
The Reaper's hounds come to claim it back!
...too late...
A wisp faded away. Another will surface.
Too many slivers lost. The Ledger stays unbalanced.
You died. Again. The Ledger notes it.
Do hurry. Wisps are terribly unpunctual.
I will pencil you in.
I will make a note of that.
Very well. I shall keep the account open. Indefinitely.
Five slivers, returned. The account balances - for now. Do try not to die so often; my quill is wearing thin.
Until our next... appointment.

quest.name: The Lone Wolf
quest.text: You walk alone. Like us.

I am Silverfang, mother of the last free pack. I have watched you hunt - always alone, always enough. Tonight is the Hunt of the Moon: men with nets and spears come for my den and my cubs. My pack is gone. I have no one... but perhaps a lone wolf would stand with a lone wolf. Guard the den stone until the moon sets. When their Huntmaster shows himself, end him.
Here is the den stone. Stay by it. Every hand they lay on it weakens the den - drive them off.
Guard the den stone until the moon sets.
Den
The cubs whimper beneath the stone.
Moon Hunters close in on the den!
Huntmaster Vrell steps out of the dark!
Step aside. That pelt is worth a fortune.
The den is undefended! Go back!
The hunters broke into the den.
You fell, and the hunters walked over you to the den.
Run with me.
The moon will rise again.
*The wolf slips back into the trees.*
*The wolf turns away and does not look back.*
The moon sets, and the cubs sleep. You are no longer a lone wolf - you are pack. Take one of my cubs' cousins; he will follow you anywhere.
Run with us, someday.

quest.name: Nightwatch
quest.text: Oi! You there - a night-walker, aren't you? I can always tell.

Ivo's the name. Lamplighter, thirty years. The shades have been getting bolder - they snuff my lamps faster than I can light them, and tonight they're out in force. You hunt in the dark like it's nothing, so maybe you'll walk with an old man? Five lamps on my round. I light them, you keep the shades off me while the flame catches. If they swarm me, the flame goes out - and so does the road.
I'll follow you. Get me to each lamp on your radar and I'll do the rest. Keep them off me while I work!
Lead Ivo to the first lamp on your radar.
Right behind you, friend. Mind the dark.
Here's one! Hold them off while I coax the flame...
The shades swarm toward Ivo!
Shades still about! Clear them before we move!
There - she's burning bright. On to the next!
Burning Bright
Lead Ivo to the next lamp.
Flame
Ivo calls out for you in the dark!
The shades snuffed Ivo's flame.
You left Ivo alone in the dark.
Lead on, then. I'll catch up.
I'll be out every night. Find me.
Suit yourself. Mind the dark.
Fine, fine. I'll manage. I always do.
Five lamps, burning bright. The road's safe tonight, thanks to you. Here - a lamplighter's thanks, and a name for the night.
Mind the dark, Nightwatch.

quest.name: The Crownless King
quest.text: Hear me, kingslayer.

I am the herald of a king who has no crown and no kingdom - only pride. My liege has watched you topple his kind: great lords of the land, one after another. He calls it insolence. He calls it a challenge. His remnants will test you first. Then he will come himself, and he will not die easily. If you defeat him, his hoard is yours.
Do not seek him. He will seek you. Survive his remnants, then face the King - and if he runs, follow him to his hall.
The Crownless King's remnants are coming for you.
Banners on the horizon...
The King's remnants attack!
The remnants fall. Their king will not be pleased.
A herald's horn sounds. The King is coming.
Kneel, and I may let you keep your head.
The Crownless King has come!
A king does not let his quarry walk away.
Enough! To my hall!
The King retreats to his hall! Follow your radar before his wounds close.
Here, in my hall, I am still king!
The King will be... delighted.
His Majesty is not accustomed to waiting.
I shall tell His Majesty you were busy.
His Majesty will consider that a surrender.
The Crownless King has fallen at last. As promised, his hoard is yours, kingslayer.
Long live... no one.

quest.name: Bounty of the Lawless
quest.text: Ha. I know that look. You hunt the hunters.

Name's Garrick. I chased murderers for forty years before my knees gave out. You've been doing my old job - putting down the ones with blood on their names. Here's what you don't know: those killers are supplied by a bandit lord who moves his coin and orders through couriers. Three of them are on the road today. Catch them before they reach the hideout, and we cut his network at the knees.
Your radar follows each courier. They walk; you run. Don't let more than one slip through.
Watch your radar for the first courier.
A courier is on the road! Your radar marks him.
The courier made it to the hideout! Don't let the next one through.
Courier down.
Too many couriers got through. The network holds.
Good hunting.
They'll be back on the road. They always are.
Kids these days.
Your call. Bandits'll thank you.
Three couriers, three satchels of letters. With these, the bandit lord's whole network unravels. You'd have made a fine bounty hunter. Here - that's yours now.
Good hunting, Bounty Hunter.

quest.name: The Cartographer's Last Map

landmark.name: Ivory Tower
landmark.riddle: Where wizards climb toward the stars but never leave their pale home, stand at its foot.
landmark.hint: The tower of the magi, between Oren and Aden.

landmark.name: Cruma Tower
landmark.riddle: An old tower sinks into the marsh; in its halls the machines still remember their makers. Stand at its door.

landmark.name: Giran Harbor
landmark.riddle: Where ships unload the riches of the world for the richest town of the kingdom.

landmark.name: Singing Waterfall
landmark.riddle: On the island where every journey begins, the water sings as it falls.

landmark.name: Valley of Saints
landmark.riddle: Holy men were laid to rest in a valley where stone angels still keep watch, not far from the town of the wind.

landmark.name: Forest of Mirrors
landmark.riddle: A forest where every tree shows you a stranger wearing your face.

landmark.name: Frozen Waterfall
landmark.riddle: A river that stopped in the middle of its fall, in the frozen north.

landmark.name: Garden of Eva
landmark.riddle: The water goddess keeps a garden under the sea. Stand at its gate.

landmark.name: Anghel Waterfall
landmark.riddle: A waterfall named for the angels, far east of the capital.
landmark.hint: East of Aden, past the Forest of Mirrors.

landmark.name: Altar of Rites
landmark.riddle: An old altar in the elves' woods where the young once proved themselves.
landmark.hint: North of Gludio, in the Windawood.

quest.text: Ah... a traveller. A real one. I can tell by your boots.

I am Ysolde, and I drew the maps your merchants still sell. My last map was never finished: three places I could never find again, written only as riddles in my old hand. My eyes are too weak now. You have walked every road in this kingdom - you might know the places I mean. Stand where each riddle points, and my map will be whole.

Here is the first riddle. Read it again any time with the question mark. If a riddle stumps you for long, my map will begin to show you the way. Teleport, walk, swim - however you like. Dying will not stop you.
Yes... yes! Just as I drew it, long ago.
The map shifts. Another riddle appears.
A faint mark appears on your map...
Bring my map home.
The map has waited forty years. It can wait a little more.
Perhaps another traveller, then.
Then my map dies with me.
My map is whole again. I can rest. Take this - and the title of a fellow cartographer.
May every road you take lead somewhere worth going.

quest.name: The Gilded Curse
quest.text: Gold. I smell so much gold on you.

Do not be afraid. I am only a ghost - a merchant who loved gold more than life, and kept it after. Now I cannot spend it, cannot carry it, cannot let it go. You carry a fortune too; you understand. My mule is loaded with my last treasure. Lead her to the five waystones where I made my offerings, and stand guard while she rests - every bandit for leagues can smell that gold. If they rob her, my curse stays. If not... well, a little gold rubs off on whoever helps.
She'll follow you. Get her to each waystone on your radar and keep the bandits' hands off her packs.
Lead the mule to the first waystone on your radar.
*The mule snorts and falls in behind you, packs jingling.*
*The mule stops by the waystone to rest. Bandits converge!*
Bandits go for the gold!
Bandits still lurking! Drive them off!
*The mule shakes her packs, ready to go.*
Offering Made
Lead the mule to the next waystone.
Gold
The mule is alone with the gold!
The bandits stripped the mule's packs bare.
You left the mule - and the gold - behind.
Mind the packs. Every coin.
Gold can wait. Gold always waits.
You will regret walking away from gold. I did.
Then may your gold weigh on you as mine did.
Every coin offered at last. The curse is lifted... and look: the gold has left its mark on you. It suits you.
Spend it. Spend it all. Trust me.

quest.name: The Unbroken

echo.name: You, Who Never Fell
echo.line: I am what you would be, if you never had to try.

echo.name: You, Who Never Doubted
echo.line: Doubt is a door. I walked through it.

quest.text: Do you recognise me? You will.

I am you - the you of some tomorrow. You have climbed so far without falling once. Do you know how rare that is? It has made you something the world did not expect, and the world will test it. Better I test it first. Face four shadows of who you might become. Beat them, and you stay unbroken.
They come one at a time, right here. Do not leave this place. Do not fall.
Every breath you take to rest, I take too.
You ran from yourself. That never works.
So you can break after all. Get up. Try again another day.
Show me.
I know where you will be. I always do.
Funny. I remember walking away, too.
Then I will become someone else.
You beat every version of yourself. Good. Stay unbroken - for both of us.
See you tomorrow.

quest.name: The Gravedigger's Debt
quest.text: You've a grave-smell on you, friend. Don't take it wrong.

Hollis. I dig the graves round these parts, and I've dug more this year than in the twenty before. You've been sending the walking dead back where they belong - I've noticed; they come in quieter. But four old graves won't stay shut. Something keeps pulling the dead back up. Go to each grave, put down whatever climbs out, and say the old words over it. Sit and pray, quiet-like. That seals it.
First grave's on your radar. They'll climb out when you get close. Put them down, then kneel and pray.
Find the first restless grave on your radar.
The earth heaves. The dead climb out!
The grave won't settle while its dead still walk. Put them down.
The grave settles. Silence.
Another grave stirs. Follow your radar.
Mind your step out there.
The dead aren't going anywhere. Well. They are. That's the problem.
Busy, eh? So are the dead.
I'll fetch a bigger shovel, then.
Four graves, sealed. I'll sleep tonight for the first time in a month. Here - I owe you.
Rest easy. You've earned it.

quest.name: The Old Banner
quest.text: Soldier. Stand easy.

Commander Brenna, of a regiment no one remembers. You have won glory on the fields where we bled - I can see it on you. Every year on this day the phantom army of the old war rises to take our banner. Every year there are fewer of us to hold it. This year there is only me... and maybe you. Plant the banner with me and hold it until the phantoms break.
The banner stands. Hold this ground. If the phantoms touch it, it weakens - don't let them.
Hold the banner until the phantom army breaks.
Banner
The old banner snaps in a wind that isn't there.
Phantom soldiers advance on the banner!
The Phantom Siege Lord takes the field!
That rag has flown long enough.
The banner stands alone! Back to it!
The phantoms tore the banner down.
Regiment, form up!
The phantoms rise every year. I'll find you before the next.
Dismissed, then.
Then the regiment ends with me.
The banner holds - one more year. The regiment lives as long as someone remembers. Carry it with you, banner-bearer.
Regiment! Salute!
